description: Hi! I'm from Peru 🇵🇪, and I'm passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation. I'm participating in NASA Space Apps to challenge myself and learn new things. My team's challenge is to create a map of Mars! I'm excited to collaborate, share ideas, and build something amazing! 🚀
summary:
MARSWALK — Explore smarter. Walk safer. Discover more.

MARSWALK is an interactive Martian exploration and mission-planning interface concept focused on Gale Crater and Mount Sharp. It aims to bring different scientific perspectives of Mars into one visual environment, including orbital imagery, topographic information, geological resources, and rover observations.

Through a futuristic navigation interface, users can explore a schematic Martian map, visualize proposed routes, identify scientific points of interest, and examine different information layers. MARSWALK addresses the challenge of helping future astronauts better understand unfamiliar terrain and make more informed exploration decisions.

Its potential impact is to make planetary science more accessible and demonstrate how robotic exploration data could support future human missions to Mars.

Developed independently in Pucallpa, Peru, MARSWALK is an early prototype that illustrates this vision through an interactive web experience.
details:
MARSWALK — Explore smarter. Walk safer. Discover more.

What does the project do and how does it work?

MARSWALK is a concept for an interactive Martian exploration and mission-planning interface. Its goal is to help future astronauts understand the Martian surface by bringing different scientific perspectives together in one visual environment.

The project focuses on Gale Crater and Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), the region explored by NASA's Curiosity rover.

The proposed interface allows users to explore a schematic Martian map, visualize an exploration route, identify scientific points of interest, and switch between information layers such as terrain, geology, and navigation.

Its intended workflow is: observe the terrain, interpret scientific information, identify areas of interest, and plan an exploration route while considering potential risks.

What are its benefits?

MARSWALK aims to make complex planetary information easier to understand and use.

Its potential benefits include:

  • Bringing different types of Mars exploration information into one interface.
  • Helping users visualize terrain and geological features.
  • Supporting the identification of scientific exploration targets.
  • Encouraging safer and more informed route-planning decisions.
  • Making planetary science more accessible through an intuitive visual experience.

What is the expected impact?

MARSWALK explores how decades of robotic Mars exploration could support future human missions.

By organizing orbital observations, topographic information, geological resources, and rover imagery into a unified exploration concept, the project could help bridge the gap between scientific data and practical surface exploration.

Our long-term vision is to make planetary exploration information more understandable, accessible, and useful for future explorers.

What tools and technologies were used?

The prototype was developed as a web-based interface concept using:

  • HTML5: Interface structure.
  • CSS3: Visual design, layout, animations, and futuristic styling.
  • JavaScript: Interactive elements, map markers, layer controls, and interface behavior.
  • NASA and USGS scientific resources: Research references for the proposed data layers, including HiRISE, CTX, CRISM, MOLA, Curiosity rover observations, and planetary geological maps.

The project is designed as a lightweight web experience that can be accessed through a browser.

What makes the project creative?

MARSWALK combines the idea of a futuristic astronaut navigation tablet with an accessible planetary exploration interface.

Instead of presenting Mars information as disconnected scientific resources, it proposes organizing different perspectives around a single exploration experience.

Its visual design, interactive controls, mission-planning workflow, and focus on human exploration aim to make the experience intuitive and engaging.

What factors were considered?

The project considers several factors relevant to future human exploration:

  • Terrain characteristics and elevation.
  • Geological and scientific interest.
  • Potential obstacles and uncertain surface conditions.
  • Astronaut mobility and spacesuit limitations.
  • Route planning and return strategies.
  • The importance of combining information from different scientific missions.

Current prototype limitations: MARSWALK is an early conceptual prototype. Its displayed map, routes, astronaut position, waypoints, and hazard indicators are illustrative, not validated navigation data. The NASA and USGS resources listed above provide the scientific foundation for the proposed layers, but their original datasets have not yet been fully processed and integrated into the prototype.

Project creator: Independent participant from Pucallpa, Peru.

MARSWALK — Explore smarter. Walk safer. Discover more.
